items.question: A gecko eats 70 crickets every three days.  The first day she eats 30% of the crickets.  The second day she eats 6 less than the first, and the third day she finishes up the remaining crickets.  How many crickets does she eat on the third day?

previous_f3_program: collection("gecko.three_day_crickets", "cricket", "gecko.three_day_cycle", source("70 crickets every three days"))
observe(at("gecko.three_day_crickets.count", "initial"), 70, "count", source("70 crickets every three days"))
observe(at("gecko.cricket_cycle.duration", "current"), 3, "day", source("every three days"))

consume("first_day_consumption", "gecko", at("gecko.three_day_crickets.count", "current"), fraction(at("gecko.three_day_crickets.count", "initial"), 30, 100), source("The first day she eats 30% of the crickets"))
offset("gecko.three_day_crickets.consumed.second_day.count", event_field("first_day_consumption", "quantity"), -6, "count", source("The second day she eats 6 less than the first"))

consume("second_day_consumption", "gecko", at("gecko.three_day_crickets.count", "current"), "gecko.three_day_crickets.consumed.second_day.count", source("The second day she eats 6 less than the first"))

consume("third_day_consumption", "gecko", at("gecko.three_day_crickets.count", "current"), at("gecko.three_day_crickets.count", "current"), source("the third day she finishes up the remaining crickets"))
query("value", event_field("third_day_consumption", "quantity"))

items.question: Marcus has received a commission for as many paintings as possible. Marcus plans out his drawings so that his client can receive some of the paintings as soon as possible but it is still going to take a long time. On the first day, he paints 2 paintings. He then paints every day and each day, he paints twice as many paintings as he painted the day before. If he paints for 5 days, how many paintings will he have painted in total?

previous_f3_program: collection("marcus.five_day_paintings", "painting", "five_day_period", source("On the first day, he paints 2 paintings"))
observe(at("marcus.painting_period.duration", "planned"), 5, "day", source("If he paints for 5 days"))
produce("day_1_painting", "marcus", at("marcus.five_day_paintings.count", "current"), 2, source("On the first day, he paints 2 paintings"))

produce("day_2_painting", "marcus", at("marcus.five_day_paintings.count", "current"), scale(event_field("day_1_painting", "quantity"), 2), source("each day, he paints twice as many paintings as he painted the day before"))

produce("day_3_painting", "marcus", at("marcus.five_day_paintings.count", "current"), scale(event_field("day_2_painting", "quantity"), 2), source("each day, he paints twice as many paintings as he painted the day before"))

produce("day_4_painting", "marcus", at("marcus.five_day_paintings.count", "current"), scale(event_field("day_3_painting", "quantity"), 2), source("each day, he paints twice as many paintings as he painted the day before"))

produce("day_5_painting", "marcus", at("marcus.five_day_paintings.count", "current"), scale(event_field("day_4_painting", "quantity"), 2), source("each day, he paints twice as many paintings as he painted the day before"))
query("value", at("marcus.five_day_paintings.count", "current"))

items.question: UF got into the national championship. For them to get into the championship, they scored a total of 720 points during their previous 24 games.  In the championship game, however, their opponent was much stronger than any other team they had previously gone against and they scored 2 points less than half as much as they had previously scored in each of the 24 games. Their opponent only lost by 2 points.  How many points did their opponent score?

previous_f3_program: observe(at("uf.points.total", "previous_24_games"), 720, "point", source("a total of 720 points during their previous 24 games"))
observe(at("uf.games.count", "previous_24_games"), 24, "count", source("their previous 24 games"))

rate_relation(at("uf.points.total", "previous_24_games"), at("uf.points.per_game", "previous_24_games"), at("uf.games.count", "previous_24_games"), source("a total of 720 points during their previous 24 games"))

fraction_of(at("uf.points.half_previous_per_game", "championship_game"), at("uf.points.per_game", "previous_24_games"), 1, 2, source("half as much as they had previously scored in each of the 24 games"))

offset(at("uf.points", "championship_game"), at("uf.points.half_previous_per_game", "championship_game"), -2, "point", source("they scored 2 points less than half as much as they had previously scored in each of the 24 games"))
offset(at("uf.opponent.points", "championship_game"), at("uf.points", "championship_game"), -2, "point", source("Their opponent only lost by 2 points"))
query("value", at("uf.opponent.points", "championship_game"))

items.question: Nellie can eat 12 sourball candies before crying. Jacob can only manage half of that number of candies, and Lana can only do three fewer than Jacob. They had a bucket of 30 candies, and all of them ate until they cried. If they divide the remaining candies in the bucket equally, how many sourball candies will they each get?

previous_f3_program: collection("bucket.candies", "candy", "bucket", source("a bucket of 30 candies"))
collection("candy_eaters", "person", "group", source("all of them ate until they cried"))
member("candy_eaters", "nellie", source("Nellie can eat 12 sourball candies before crying"))
member("candy_eaters", "jacob", source("Jacob can only manage half of that number of candies"))
member("candy_eaters", "lana", source("Lana can only do three fewer than Jacob"))
observe(at("nellie.sourball_candies.crying_threshold.count", "current"), 12, "count", source("Nellie can eat 12 sourball candies before crying"))

fraction_of(at("jacob.sourball_candies.crying_threshold.count", "current"), at("nellie.sourball_candies.crying_threshold.count", "current"), 1, 2, source("Jacob can only manage half of that number of candies"))
offset(at("lana.sourball_candies.crying_threshold.count", "current"), at("jacob.sourball_candies.crying_threshold.count", "current"), -3, "count", source("Lana can only do three fewer than Jacob"))
observe(at("bucket.candies.count", "initial"), 30, "count", source("a bucket of 30 candies"))
consume("nellie_eats_until_crying", "nellie", at("bucket.candies.count", "current"), at("nellie.sourball_candies.crying_threshold.count", "current"), source("all of them ate until they cried"))
consume("jacob_eats_until_crying", "jacob", at("bucket.candies.count", "current"), at("jacob.sourball_candies.crying_threshold.count", "current"), source("all of them ate until they cried"))
consume("lana_eats_until_crying", "lana", at("bucket.candies.count", "current"), at("lana.sourball_candies.crying_threshold.count", "current"), source("all of them ate until they cried"))

quotient_relation(at("candy_eaters.remaining_candy_share.count", "current"), at("bucket.candies.count", "current"), at("candy_eaters.count", "current"), source("divide the remaining candies in the bucket equally"))
query("value", at("candy_eaters.remaining_candy_share.count", "current"))

items.question: The country of Belize had a 5 lane bridge that had 2000 vehicles passing through it every month. They decided to build a new bridge that had twice the capacity of the old one, and the number of vehicles passing through the new one increased by 60% more than the old bridge. If the bridges work concurrently for a year, calculate the total number of vehicles that pass through the two bridges.
